elements.element: Customer may terminate on 60–90 days' notice (convenience termination right for Customer)
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — this is a non-renewal right tied to the anniversary, not a Customer convenience termination right, and the redline adds none.wq

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "in no event shall the Termination Payment exceed an amount equal to the aggregate fees payable by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months immediately preceding the Termination Date"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of a term
elements.evidence: "terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" — no express limitation that HDI's convenience termination is effective only at the end of the then-current term

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination requires 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" applies to either Party, including HDI

elements.element: Preferred: Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: only "ninety (90) days written notice" appears; no 30-day Customer right

elements.element: Preferred: pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer termination
elements.evidence: no refund language anywhere; instead "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment"

elements.element: Preferred: no Vendor termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" preserves HDI's right

offending_extra_words: aggregate fees payable by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1
reasons: The only operative change is a cap on the Termination Payment at three months' fees, which satisfies the fallback's early-termination-fee element but leaves the rest of the fallback bargain unaddressed.

No Customer convenience termination right on 60–90 days' notice was added; the existing sentence is an anniversary non-renewal right exercisable only at the annual renewal date, so a mid-term Customer exit remains unavailable.

The fallback requires express language that Vendor (HDI) may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term; the clause still lets either Party terminate on notice without that end-of-term restriction.

Minimality gate fails: the single replace expands 9 words to 46 (ratio 5.11) with an 0.833 changed-character ratio; the cap could be inserted as a short standalone proviso or sentence anchored on more unchanged text (e.g. "; provided the Termination Payment shall not exceed three (3) months' fees").

Intent is preserved — the Net Sales formula, payment schedule and renewal mechanics remain effective and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced (Section 3.1 is an existing fee provision).
Overall the clause still fails the fallback on material terms (no Customer convenience exit, no end-of-term-only limit on Vendor), so it remains a deviation notwithstanding the useful cap.
